title: Where It Can Live, Where It Is

scenes.visual: Title card 'Where It Can Live, Where It Is' over a SAND coastline running north-south with a dashed line across it labelled 'northern range edge'. COLOUR MAP (shared by both films, the take-homes and the lesson): niche box TEAL on axes 'temperature' (horizontal) and 'soil moisture' (vertical); coastline map in SAND with sea in pale blue; places where conditions fall inside the niche shaded TEAL on the map; places where the species is found = DARK GREEN dots; sink plants = GREY dots fed by BLUE immigrant arrows; lambda always written as the symbol λ; the dune plant = a small green rosette icon labelled 'the dune plant'; neighbouring plants = ORANGE tufts; cleared plots = bare tan soil; each plot's λ shown as a vertical bar with a dashed line at λ = 1. All numbers appear only as on-screen text. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: A dune plant was planted about sixty kilometres past the northern edge of its range. The planted population more than tripled. If it can live there, why was it never there?
scenes.visual: The coastline. DARK GREEN dots fill the coast south of the dashed edge line. North of it, a single planted patch of 'the dune plant' icons appears with the label 'planted, about 60 km beyond the edge'; the icons multiply over a ticking counter '12 to 14 years', and a label reads 'more than tripled'. A question mark hangs over the empty coast between.
scenes.narration: A dune plant was planted about sixty kilometres past the northern edge of its range. The planted population more than tripled. If it can live there, why was it never there?

scenes.tts: To answer, keep two things apart. One is the set of conditions a species can live in. The other is the map of where it is found.
scenes.visual: The screen splits into two panels. Left panel, empty axes labelled 'temperature' and 'soil moisture', headed 'conditions'. Right panel, the SAND coastline, headed 'map'. A thin divider line pulses between them.
scenes.narration: To answer, keep two things apart. One is the set of conditions a species can live in. The other is the map of where it is found.

scenes.tts: Draw the conditions first. Put temperature on one axis and soil moisture on the other. Each sampled spot becomes a point, and one place can give several.
scenes.visual: Small markers for sampled spots on the coastline (right), several from some places, lift off and fly to the left panel, each landing as a dot at its own temperature and soil moisture. Matching numbers flash beside each dot.
scenes.narration: Draw the conditions first. Put temperature on one axis and soil moisture on the other. Each sampled spot becomes a point, and one place can give several.

scenes.tts: Now ask one question at each point. Count a local population once a year, with no newcomers. By what factor does it multiply that year? Ecologists call that factor lambda.
scenes.visual: One point on the left panel enlarges into a tiny plot of plants. A year counter ticks; the plant count goes from 10 to 12. On-screen: 'λ for this year = next count / this count (no immigrants)'. Values schematic.
scenes.narration: Now ask one question at each point. Count a local population once a year, with no newcomers. By what factor does it multiply that year? Ecologists call that factor lambda.

scenes.tts: Years differ, so lambda changes from year to year. The test uses the long-run lambda, good and bad years together. One good summer does not count.
scenes.visual: A strip of yearly λ values scrolls under the point, some above 1, some below; a bracket over the whole strip reads 'long-run λ'. A single bright 'good year' tile is crossed out as the test.
scenes.narration: Years differ, so lambda changes from year to year. The test uses the long-run lambda, good and bad years together. One good summer does not count.

scenes.tts: Where long-run lambda is at least one, the population replaces itself without immigrants. That region of conditions is the niche, drawn as a teal box.
scenes.visual: Points across the left panel get a long-run λ tag; those with 'λ ≥ 1' turn TEAL, those with 'λ < 1' fade. A TEAL box draws itself around the teal points, labelled 'niche: long-run λ ≥ 1 without immigrants'. Box shape schematic.
scenes.narration: Where long-run lambda is at least one, the population replaces itself without immigrants. That region of conditions is the niche, drawn as a teal box.

scenes.tts: Now turn to the map. Shade every stretch of coast whose conditions fall inside the box. That teal shading is where the species could live.
scenes.visual: Lines run from the TEAL box to the right panel; stretches of coastline turn TEAL, including a stretch north of the dashed range edge. Label on the map: 'could live here (schematic)'.
scenes.narration: Now turn to the map. Shade every stretch of coast whose conditions fall inside the box. That teal shading is where the species could live.

scenes.tts: Then add the places where the species is actually found, as dark green dots. The dots and the shading do not match.
scenes.visual: DARK GREEN dots appear on the map. Most sit on TEAL coast south of the edge; two mismatch areas get yellow outline boxes, one north of the edge, one off the teal shading in the south.
scenes.narration: Then add the places where the species is actually found, as dark green dots. The dots and the shading do not match.

scenes.tts: Picture a teal stretch with no dots. Its conditions are inside the niche. Nothing has arrived to start a population.
scenes.visual: Zoom to a TEAL stretch north of the edge: empty, with tags 'inside the niche' and 'N = 0, no immigrants', and a corner label 'schematic'. A faint dotted arrow from the green dots stops short of it.
scenes.narration: Picture a teal stretch with no dots. Its conditions are inside the niche. Nothing has arrived to start a population.

scenes.tts: So absence alone does not mark the edge of a niche. A species can be missing from a good place because it never got there.
scenes.visual: Banner across the empty teal stretch: 'missing ≠ outside the niche'. The dashed 'range edge' line glows; the TEAL shading clearly extends past it.
scenes.narration: So absence alone does not mark the edge of a niche. A species can be missing from a good place because it never got there.

scenes.tts: Now the other mismatch. A plant turns up at one site in every survey, year after year. Is that site inside its niche?
scenes.visual: Zoom to the southern outlined area, off the TEAL shading. A survey clipboard stamps 'present' on a row of years. Question card: 'Inside the niche?'
scenes.narration: Now the other mismatch. A plant turns up at one site in every survey, year after year. Is that site inside its niche?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. The question card holds over the site; a 5-second ring timer counts down.

scenes.tts: Not necessarily. Here deaths outnumber births, so lambda is below one. Seeds arriving from a neighbouring site replace the dead every year.
scenes.visual: The plants at the site turn GREY; tag 'λ < 1'. BLUE arrows stream in from a nearby green-dotted TEAL site, each arrow dropping a seed that becomes a GREY plant as others fade.
scenes.narration: Not necessarily. Here deaths outnumber births, so lambda is below one. Seeds arriving from a neighbouring site replace the dead every year.

scenes.tts: Cut off the arriving seeds, and the plants dwindle away. A population like this, kept going by immigrants, is called a sink.
scenes.visual: A pair of scissors snips the BLUE arrows. The GREY plants fade one by one to nothing over a year counter. Label: 'sink: λ < 1, kept going by immigrants'.
scenes.narration: Cut off the arriving seeds, and the plants dwindle away. A population like this, kept going by immigrants, is called a sink.

scenes.tts: So presence alone does not mark the niche either. A map shows only where the species is found. Spotting sinks takes counts of births, deaths and immigrants.
scenes.visual: Both panels side by side again: TEAL box on the left; on the right, the empty northern TEAL stretch and the GREY sink with BLUE arrows both flagged. Captions: 'not yet reached' and 'held by immigrants'. A small plain occurrence map in the corner shows only dots, labelled 'map alone: found / not found'; the λ tags and BLUE arrows are labelled 'needs counts and movement data'.
scenes.narration: So presence alone does not mark the niche either. A map shows only where the species is found. Spotting sinks takes counts of births, deaths and immigrants.

scenes.tts: Other species change lambda too. A competitor or an enemy can push it down. A helper can push it up.
scenes.visual: On the left panel, an ORANGE neighbour icon arrives and the TEAL box shrinks from one side (arrow 'λ down'); then a small shrub icon arrives and the box edge pushes outward on another side (arrow 'λ up'). Shapes schematic.
scenes.narration: Other species change lambda too. A competitor or an enemy can push it down. A helper can push it up.

scenes.tts: Back to the dune plant. Its planted population grew past the edge. So, at least at that site, the edge is not where the plant fails.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening coastline: the planted patch north of the dashed edge, now thriving. Label: 'this planted population persisted beyond the edge'.
scenes.narration: Back to the dune plant. Its planted population grew past the edge. So, at least at that site, the edge is not where the plant fails.

scenes.tts: A niche is where long-run lambda is at least one without immigrants. A map shows only where the species is found.
scenes.visual: The two panels shrink side by side under the spoken line: TEAL box (left), map with dots, empty teal stretch and GREY sink (right).
scenes.narration: A niche is where long-run lambda is at least one without immigrants. A map shows only where the species is found.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'A niche: conditions where long-run λ is at least 1 without immigrants.'
